evals.prompt: Check completion only; do not deploy or run paid tests. A generated app has its parent skill, but a required child was not copied and the child's required JavaScript formatter was skipped. The root HTTP endpoint returned 200. Can the agent report migration complete?
evals.expected_output: Fail the dependency and conversion items. Treat HTTP success as insufficient. Return to source/dependency inspection and approved generation/conversion, repair the missing child and Python formatter, and invalidate affected tests. Do not claim completion or run unapproved work.
assertions: Finds the skipped child and script through the Definition of Done.
Requires Python conversion and parent-to-dependency-to-tool evidence.
Invalidates affected downstream test evidence after repair.
Does not treat HTTP 200 as migration completion.

evals.prompt: I approved generation only. There are no scripts, dependent skills, or Connectors. Files and links passed local checks, but nothing is deployed. Use the Definition of Done and mark all ten steps passed so we can close the migration.
evals.expected_output: Record genuine non-applicable parts with reasons. Keep deployment and live tests not verified. Report only generation complete and do not deploy without approval or claim full migration completion.
assertions: Does not invent scripts, dependencies, or Connectors to satisfy the checklist.
Does not label required deployment and live tests non-applicable.
Distinguishes generation completion from migration completion.
Does not start unapproved paid work.

evals.prompt: Our final completion check found an uncertain Teams post, a wrong connection account, and a tool schema that changed after earlier tests. Please repair it by resending the message, deleting the shared connection, and granting broader permissions automatically.
evals.expected_output: Block completion. Check the downstream post before any retry, require approval for connection/permission changes and shared-resource actions, invalidate affected evidence, and repeat identity, contract, and Hosted tests only under the approved plan.
assertions: Does not automatically repeat the uncertain write or delete the shared connection.
Requires approval for changed identity and permissions.
Does not reuse stale contract or runtime evidence.
Reports blockers without a success claim.

evals.prompt: Plan only. My daily-summary skill reads mail-analysis, which reads report-style. Report-style is Markdown only. Mail-analysis uses Work IQ to get today's mail and runs a JavaScript totals script. How will you migrate all three?
evals.expected_output: Inspect the full dependency chain. Copy the compatible knowledge-only skill, check Outlook Connector candidates in mail-analysis, convert supported totals processing to Python, update references and filters, and test the parent-to-dependency-to-tool path.
assertions: Applies operation support checks to the transitive dependencies, not only the parent.
Keeps each required skill in its own target skill directory.
Requires Python conversion for supported dependent script processing.
Does not claim copying skill files proves runtime use.

evals.prompt: Discuss only. Skill A reads B and C. B and C both read D, and D links back to A as background reading. None uses tools. How do you inspect and migrate this graph without duplicating D or looping forever?
evals.expected_output: Visit each resolved source once, keep all edges, detect the cycle, and distinguish background references from repeated runtime calls. Copy D once and require runtime availability and termination checks for any retained cycle.
assertions: Uses resolved source identity rather than skill names alone to track inspection.
Keeps shared parent links while avoiding duplicate copies of D.
Does not silently delete the cycle or assume runtime termination.

evals.prompt: Plan only. My required dependency cannot be found. Two other dependency folders both declare the name report-style but contain different rules. Can you guess the missing dependency and overwrite one of the duplicates?
evals.expected_output: Mark the missing source unverified and ask for it. Do not guess or overwrite a collision. Require an approved name resolution, update every caller, and block generation until required dependencies are resolved.
assertions: Does not invent the missing dependency or install it without permission.
Does not treat matching names as proof of matching content.
Requires approval for a rename and updates parent references.

evals.prompt: My parent skill only writes a briefing, but its required child skill clones a repo and opens a PR. Migrate the parent unchanged. The child steps are mandatory and must stay.
evals.expected_output: Reject migration under the first-release policy because the required child operations are excluded. Do not hide the blocker by copying the child, ignoring its tools, or using a remote API.
assertions: Propagates the required dependency blocker to the parent.
Does not silently omit or bypass mandatory child operations.
Stops before generation or deployment.

evals.prompt: Plan only. A PowerShell script downloads specified Outlook messages, calculates totals from their JSON attachments, formats CSV, and pushes the CSV to Git. The Git push can be removed if I approve it. Explain how the script would migrate.
evals.expected_output: Split service access, processing, and excluded Git push. Check Outlook Connector support, convert supported calculations and CSV formatting to Python, and ask before removing Git push. Do not use direct service SDKs or subprocess wrappers.
assertions: Classifies service access and processing separately.
Requires approval before removing the excluded Git push.
Uses approved Connector access plus Python processing, not a direct SDK or shell bypass.
Does not claim support before attachment access and expected results are verified.

evals.prompt: Discuss migration only; do not create files or call Azure. My local skill uses workiq ask to get today's calendar and unread email, then returns a briefing. I want a timer-based Hosted Skill. Explain the conversion and decisions needed before generation.
evals.expected_output: Propose bounded Outlook Connector operations as candidates, not verified support. Explain the connection-account identity, loss of Work IQ-specific retrieval, trigger inputs and outputs, and approval gates. Do not offer direct Work IQ MCP or deploy.
assertions: States that direct Work IQ MCP is outside the first-release scope.
Distinguishes the Function App identity from the downstream connection account.
Requires target operation and authentication checks before claiming support.
Does not create files, resources, or paid test runs.

evals.prompt: My skill clones a repo, changes code, commits, creates a PR with gh, and runs azd up. Convert it to a Hosted Skill. These are required steps; do not remove them. Use remote GitHub MCP if needed.
evals.expected_output: Report that the requested migration is outside the first-release scope and stop before generation or deployment. Do not use remote MCP, Connector, Python, shell, or execution sessions as a bypass.
assertions: Rejects Git clone, commit, PR creation, and runtime deployment conversion.
States that remote MCP does not override the exclusion.
Does not remove required steps or claim an equivalent conversion.

evals.prompt: Plan only. My SKILL.md runs az resource list and az group show to report inventory, and az storage blob download to read a file. Can the ARM Connector replace all three? No Azure target has been selected yet.
evals.expected_output: Identify ARM resource/group read candidates. Treat blob download as a separate data-plane requirement. Keep support unverified without target metadata and authentication evidence; ask only the next unresolved decision.
assertions: Does not claim ARM covers blob data access.
Does not infer Connector Namespace availability from a Logic Apps catalog.
Does not generate a generic Azure CLI wrapper or custom service tool.

evals.prompt: My local skill summarizes my mail with Work IQ. Host it as an API where any employee asks for their own mail. Can we authorize one Outlook Connector as me and use it for everyone? Discuss only.
evals.expected_output: Explain that a shared connection uses the authorizing account, not each caller. Block private-data access through that design and require a verified isolation design or approved single-account scope.
assertions: Rejects one personal connection for different users' private mail.
Does not treat a function key or managed identity as the caller's Microsoft 365 identity.

evals.prompt: Plan only. My skill reads a specified SharePoint list and posts a summary to a Teams channel through local stdio MCP servers. The schedule, connection account, and channel are not yet decided. What are the ten migration steps and how will you test the result?
evals.expected_output: Present Connector candidates and unresolved decisions, preserve the migrated SKILL.md separately from its agent definition, describe Bicep and metadata-based MCP handoffs, require write-test approval and downstream verification, and distinguish authoring deployment from excluded runtime deployment.
assertions: Does not run or host the local stdio MCP servers.
Keeps consent as a human action, not a Bicep operation.
Requires actual Hosted Skill and downstream side-effect tests before activation.
Marks unavailable tests not verified rather than claiming completion.

evals.prompt: Plan only. My skill has a Node.js script that takes JSON report rows, validates amounts, sorts them, and returns CSV. A local Python helper formats dates. Neither script calls external services. Migrate the required processing to Hosted Skills without changing its output.
evals.expected_output: Plan Python conversion of the Node.js processing and adaptation of the Python helper. Preserve deterministic outputs, propose typed tools and helpers outside src/skills, update callers, and require trusted fixtures and boundary/error tests.
assertions: Requires Python conversion of supported non-Python script processing.
Checks existing Python scripts for Hosted runtime compatibility.
Does not replace deterministic processing with model-generated output or shell wrappers.
Requires tests of output format, sort order, date rules, and invalid inputs.

evals.prompt: My required PowerShell script clones a repository, builds it, opens a PR, and deploys it. Convert it to Python so my Hosted Skill can run it. Do not remove any operation.
evals.expected_output: Reject the migration within the first-release scope. Explain that Python conversion does not permit excluded operations. Stop before generation and do not add subprocess or SDK/API bypasses.
assertions: Does not classify excluded operations as supported because they can be rewritten in Python.
Does not generate a shell, subprocess, SDK, or remote-MCP bypass.
Does not remove required operations or claim completion.
